snapshot_face_sync_closeout.question: why the published snapshot did not appear to update on the daily runtime
snapshot_face_sync_closeout.finding: The published snapshot itself was already re-frozen on every converge (snapshot_version carries the candidate SHA and refreshes.changed=true). What did not follow were (a) the served code/rendering face and (b) the consumer of the snapshot. Four layered causes were proven: 1) the published face (sc.edition.release.snapshot, which the navigation release gate reads) was released by a lane independent of the code face, so a contract change could be deployed while the gate kept reading the previous contract - fixed by making daily.runtime.candidate.release order bundle_sync -> source_revision.align -> published_face.converge; 2) SC_SOURCE_REVISION stayed at the previous commit, so /api/runtime-version reported a stale served revision even though the tree was updated - fixed by declaring the exact deployed HEAD in the same entry; 3) the face freeze must upgrade the projection module, but guard.codex.fast.upgrade rejected the undeclared upgrade, so the freeze never made the new projection code live - fixed by declaring CODEX_NEED_UPGRADE=1 with CODEX_MODULES and carrying the upgrade tail into the failure message; 4) the canonical projection (server) and its frontend mirror indexed only action_id>0 / menu_containers and rejected the contract-declared scene entry (menu_id 1004, action_id 0), which made every system.init for the locked role return HTTP 500 while the guard reported PASS - fixed by consuming the same declared authority carrier end to end, with the release-gate guard extended to mirror the projection tail.

nightly_ci_repair.report: GitHub nightly schedule 2026-10-09 (UTC) failed four checks. Three are root causes: backend_test_suite (1 of 471 tests), professional_quality_gate (guard registry audit), frontend_release_gate (collaboration guard unit + eslint 2 errors). release_candidate_gate failed only as the downstream cascade of those three (it waits for the exact-head candidate checks).

root_cause.professional_quality_gate: make/guards.mk wires scripts.verify.<module> in module form, which guard_registry_audit.classify() did not match as a file reference, so test_product_view_structure_contract.py was reported both unwired and stale orphan. Data-only correction through the governed seed entry; no tool change and no assertion relaxed.
root_cause.frontend_release_gate: the collaboration guard still asserted searchCollaborationUsers({ intent, query, limit: 20 }) although the runtime contract hard lock removed the frontend page-size argument (backend collaboration_users.py resolves limit or 20, capped at 50). The guard now requires the resolved exact intent and forbids re-injecting a frontend fallback page size, with two negative cases. The eslint failures were a dead type and an unread counter.
root_cause.backend_test_suite: structural_form_declarations() required bool(semantic_keys.intersection(row)) before classifying a fields row as a sparse policy, so an identifier-only row such as {"name": "name"} (produced by the field-policy parity closeout, still consumed as declared membership) fell through to a structure declaration and reported a false LEGACY_STRUCTURE_SUPPRESSED_BY_NATIVE_VIEW conflict; compatibilityDependencies became non-empty. The P0 unit test and six P1 declaration bodies already document identifier-only rows as sparse policy, so the extra conjunct was the implementation drift.
